page: Microsoft Azure E16-4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor running at 3.35 GHz. The configuration features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. The instance includes 262 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff between massive memory capacity and processing throughput. The server exhibits poor CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks falling into the bottom 10%. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is rated as poor. Memory bandwidth is average for large-block read-only operations and PassMark memory tests, but weak for small-block cached reads and large-block writes. Computational tasks such as Geekbench ray tracing, image processing, and software compilation with Clang score in the bottom 25%, indicating that this instance is not suited for compute-intensive workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-4as_v4 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a specialized option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. Database operations under PassMark and Redis SET operations both perform in the bottom 25%, suggesting it is better suited for read-heavy caching, memory-intensive data buffering, or legacy applications requiring large memory footprints without heavy transactional processing. It is also capable of basic text processing and low-demand single-threaded tasks where its average single-core Geekbench performance is sufficient.
